(def hash (fn [o]
  (cond
    ;; A string's hash is computed directly, as JVM Clojure's String.hashCode
    ;; is (#409), by the runtime: ClojureScript's string-hash-cache, a js-obj,
    ;; costs more to search than the hash does to compute. hash-string keeps
    ;; the cache. It is tested first: no string implements IHash, since a
    ;; built-in type's core protocols can't be extended outside core.
    (string? o)
    (suss.bootstrap/string-hash o)

    (implements? IHash o)
    (bit-xor (-hash o) 0)

    (number? o)
    (suss.bootstrap/hash-number o)

    ;; note: mirrors Clojure's behavior on the JVM, where the hashCode is
    ;; 1231 for true and 1237 for false
    ;; http://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/lang/Boolean.html#hashCode%28%29
    (true? o) 1231

    (false? o) 1237

    (instance? BootstrapDate o)
    (bit-xor (.valueOf o) 0)

    (nil? o) 0

    :else
    (bit-xor (-hash o) 0))))
rationale: Retain all pinned hash branches and their source order. Fixed defn bootstrap and private numeric guards replace finite/safe-integer/floor/remainder host operations. A descriptor-backed BootstrapDate replaces host Date identity; its valueOf method reads TimeClip-normalized numeric milliseconds. No Date branch is removed. Numeric-only private construction is not general JavaScript Date syntax, parsing, calendar operations or completed Inst/equality/printing compatibility. A number hashes as Clojure's hasheq, Murmur3's hashLong for a long and Double.hashCode for a double, with -0.0 as 0.0 (#336). A string hashes through the runtime's string-hash, (m3-hash-int (hash-string* s)) computed in int32 arithmetic, the same value since m3-hash-int converts its operand with ToInt32, rather than through the pinned string-hash-cache, whose js-obj lookup costs more than computing the hash; hash-string and the cache are unchanged for direct callers (#409). The string test comes first, which gives the same result because no string implements IHash.
